rv.q: The play illustrates, with believable characters, the way grief can turn into anger, which in turn can sometimes shift uneasily between taking protest action and despair.
The politics of policing protest have left the building along with the sharper dialogue of the middle section of the play, melodrama, regrettably, crowding out drama.

The play as it stands is either too short or too long: not as concept, but when you pack in prison like a lighthouse flash and the gathering crescendo with accelerated narrative, the weight of it can evaporate.

cn.t: Webber's climate activism drama tackles timely but often-neglected political issues, earning moderate praise for its ambition and relevance despite mixed execution.
